Why does hyperkalemia cause peaked T waves?
AI
Great question. High extracellular K⁺ reduces the concentration gradient across the myocyte membrane. This accelerates early repolarization (phase 3 of the action potential) — so the T wave narrows and peaks.

Explain the difference between Type 1 and Type 2 RTA.
AI

Type 1 (Distal) RTA: the alpha-intercalated cells can't secrete H⁺ against a gradient. Urine pH stays > 5.5 even with acidosis. Associated with hypokalemia, nephrolithiasis, and bone demineralization.

Type 2 (Proximal) RTA: the proximal tubule can't reabsorb bicarbonate. The distal nephron can still acidify urine once plasma HCO₃⁻ drops low enough — so urine pH can fall < 5.5. Often seen with Fanconi syndrome.

Your keys never leave your browser unencrypted

Frequently asked questions

Everything you wanted to know — and a few things you didn't.

No. MedQ is an independent study tool. Our question bank and curriculum are aligned with the topics these exams cover, but we are not endorsed by or affiliated with any licensing body. Names like "USMLE" and "MRCP" are trademarks of their respective organizations.

No. The Free and Pro tiers use MedQ-provided AI models — just sign up and start studying. The Premium tier adds a "Bring Your Own Key" (BYOK) option for users who want to use their own OpenAI, Anthropic, or other provider keys. BYOK keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and never leave your account.

A traditional Q-bank gives you questions and explanations — and stops there. MedQ builds a feedback loop: every answer feeds into your weak-area model, your daily plan, your flashcard deck, and your next case simulation. The AI tutor adapts in real time, so time spent studying is always targeted at your specific gaps.

Yes. MedQ is a Progressive Web App (PWA). After your first load, you can install it to your home screen and use most features offline — including cached questions, flashcards, and on-device AI for basic queries. Premium AI tutor and live leaderboards require a connection.

Yes. Subscriptions cancel at the end of your current billing cycle — no questions, no retention calls. You keep access until then. Annual plans get a prorated refund within the first 14 days.

Your study history, weak-area analysis, and notes are tied to your account and never sold. BYOK API keys are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. You can export or delete all your data at any time from Settings → Privacy.

MedQ is curriculum-aligned for USMLE Step 1 & Step 2 CK, MRCP Part 1 & 2, PLAB 1 & 2, NEET-PG, COMLEX, and the Internal Medicine board exam. The Case Simulator and Oral Exam Simulator are particularly popular for Step 2 CS / PLAB 2 / OSCE-style assessments.
